Jon Maccoll has been the head coach of the Rutgers swimming & diving program since December of 2017. Maccoll has directed the Scarlet Knights to new heights in the Big Ten and holding a reputation for building a championship culture at each one of his stops.
During his career, Maccoll has been accountable for 182 All-America swims from 32 student-athletes and worked with six swimmers that went on to compete in the Olympics, with five earning gold medals at Olympic summer games. Under Maccoll's watch at Rutgers, the Scarlet Knights have achieved over 100 times and scores among the school's all-time top 10. In fact, 22 school records have been established during Maccoll's tenure, marking all but one of Rutgers' benchmarks achieved since his arrival. With Maccoll at the helm, Rutgers has captured its highest NCAA finish since 2006 and its highest point total in Big Ten history.
Since taking over the Rutgers swimming & diving program, Maccoll's Scarlet Knights have continued an upward trend in overall team performance and in reaching the podium at the Big Ten Championships. Over the last nine years, 22 individuals and 13 relay teams have reached top-eight status, including 68 finalists since 2022 and the highest team point total since joining the league at the 2023 championships.
In 2026, Rutgers' season was highlighted by a pair of All-American divers, as Katerina Hoffman (3-Meter) and Sephora Ford (Platform) were each named Second Team All-Americans. The duo was joined by Bailee Sturgill at NCAAs, marking the fifth-straight season the Scarlet Knights were represented on the national stage. Hoffman won the NCAA Zone Diving events in 1-Meter and 3-Meter, while Ford captured the NCAA Zone title on the Platform. At the Big Ten Championships, RU had six different podium finishers, with a Scarlet Knight placing as high as sixth, and Anna Vlachou recording multiple school records at the event, setting the top RU time in both the 100 Freestyle and 100 Butterfly. Rutgers six podium finishes were the most since 2023 and RU's six individual podium spots were the most since 2019.

Speedling's influence extended across national borders as well, as the longtime coach helped groom Canadian record holder Stefan Hirniak. The College of Staten Island and City University of New York graduate also coached five New Jersey state record holders who combined for a total of 26 records.
The American Swimming Coaches Association member spent the past 10 years as the head coach of the Scarlet Aquatic Club, coordinating training groups, implementing training regiments and maintaining the budget for a 170-member program. Prior to his head coaching stint, Speedling spent eight years as a full-time assistant at the Scarlet Aquatic Club.
His coaching career began in 1993 at the Village Greens Swim Club, where the Hopewell, N.J. resident got his first experience as a head coach. Speedling made the leap to high school swimming a year later, serving as the head varsity swimming coach at Moore Catholic (N.Y.) from 1994-2002.

Natasha Chikina.b:
Natasha Chikina has served as the Scarlet Knights’ diving coach since her appointment in July of 2021. Under her guidance, RU has acheived great sucess on the boards, with Scarlet Knight divers excelling throughout the season, Big Ten and NCAA competition, and international competitions.
Since her arrival, RU has had six All-American seasons from divers. Abigail Knapton was named First Team All-American in Platform in 2021 and Second Team All-American on 3-Meter in 2022. Holly Prasanto was named Second Team All-American on 1-Meter in 2024. Sephora Ford was named Second Team All-American in Platform Diving in both 2025 and 2026. Katerina Hoffman was named Second Team All-American on 3-Meter in 2026. RU has had an All-American on the boards in five of the past six years, with seven divers qualifying to compete at NCAAs overall across 2025 and 2026. Chikina's divers have earned 19 placements on RU's top-10 lists on the three diving events since her arrival in 2021.With her guidance, current Scarlet Knights Katerina Hoffman and Bailee Sturgill have excelled as members of Team USA Diving, competiting in numerous elite events on the international stage.
Chikina arrived “On The Banks” after spending 16 years as Nebraska’s head diving coach helping the Huskers claim at least one All-American distinction in each of her last six seasons along with appearances at the NCAA Championships for eight-straight years and 41 NCAA Zone qualifiers.Chikina coached two Husker divers at Olympic Trials with Abigail Knapton finishing seventh on 3-meter and fifth on platform.
In her last season, Chikina mentored Knapton to her fifth career first-team and sixth overall All-American honor in performances on both the platform and 3-meter finals in March. The results helped to give Nebraska its best NCAA placement since 2001 and the highest point total at nationals since 2000.
Chikina also guided Anna Filipcic to honorable-mention All-American status with a 10th place finish on 1-meter at the 2016 NCAA Championships. She helped the Cornhusker to the NCAA Championships in all four of her seasons as well as two Big Ten Conference runner-up performances on 1-meter 2016 and 3-meter in 2017.
During her tenure with Nebraska, Chikina also served as a team leader for the US National Diving Team at the 2019 FINA Grand Prix in Calgary, Canada and at the 2019 University Games in Naples, Italy.
Prior to working with the Cornhusker program, Chikina served as the assistant head coach at the U.S. Diving Regional Training Center from 2001-05. She coached a two-time Oklahoma state high school champion, two Junior Olympic National Team members and four Junior Olympic National qualifiers in addition to scouting, recruiting and judging competitions up to the national level. Chikina was also a member of the staff at the 2003 U.S. Diving National Training Camp, instructing junior national-level athletes in the spotting belt, trampoline and dryboard.
Chikina began her coaching career at her alma mater, the University of Southern California, as an undergraduate assistant coach in 1998-99, helping future Olympians Troy Dumais, Justin Dumais and Dorte Linder, and as an assistant coach with the Trojan Diving Club from 1998 to 2001, coaching two Junior Olympic national champions.
Chikina’s coaching career followed a stellar international and collegiate career. Competing at the 1996 Atlanta and 2000 Sydney Summer Olympic Games for her native Kazakhstan, Chikina finished 15th at the Atlanta Games and went to a ninth-place finish on the 10-meter platform in Sydney.
Additionally, Chikina competed on the international stage at the 1994 Goodwill Games, the 1996 World Championships, 1993, 1995 and 1999 World University Games and the 2000 FINA Grand Prix. She placed third at both the World Championships and FINA Grand Prix.
Between appearances at the Olympics, Chikina earned a pair of NCAA All-America honors at USC and was a two-time Pac-10 champion on 3-meter. She also placed fourth on platform at the 1998 NCAA Championships.
Chikina graduated from USC in 1999 with a bachelor’s degree in social science and communications and also received a physical education and coaching degree from the Kazakh Institute of Physical Education in Almaty, Kazakhstan, in 1996.
Chikina and her husband, Kris Hoffman, a fellow diving coach, are the proud parents of two daughters, Katerina and Sophia. Katerina is a diver for the Scarlet Knights.

Pat Malone.b:
Pat Malone joined the Rutgers women's swimming & diving staff as an assistant in July of 2024 and recently completed his second season on the staff in the 2025-2026 season.
Malone arrived "On The Banks" after spending the last three seasons as an assistant coach at UMBC. During his time with the Retrievers, the men's program captured back-to-back America East Championships in 2022 and 2023 while both the men's and women's teams combined for 36 America East champions. UMBC was also recognized with the 2024 America East Women's Swimming Rookie of the Year and America East Men's Swimmer of the Meet.
Prior to his post at UMBC, Malone served as head coach at Manhattan College for three seasons. The Jaspers captured 11 top-16 finishes at the Metro Atlantic Conference Championships while being standouts in the classroom. Manhattan was named to the CSCAA Scholar America Team every season along with 13 Jaspers selected to the 2020 MAAC Men's and Women's Swimming and Diving All-Academic Teams.
Malone also spent three seasons at Long Island University including a stint as interim head coach. While at LIU, Malone oversaw 29 top-eight performances at the NEC Championships with the program ranking in the top five in team GPA among LIU Brooklyn's athletic squads.
A Washington Township, New Jersey native, Malone was a DIII Honorable Mention All-American at Rowan University earning NJAC First-Team All-Conference honors in the 200 fly as well as second-team distinction in the 200 fly, 200 and 400 medley relays during his career. In the classroom, Malone was a three-time Academic All-American and recognized as a Rowan Scholar-Athlete and a Philadelphia Inquirer Men's Swimming Academic All-Area honoree. He also was the recipient of the Richard Wacker Award for upperclassmen leadership as a team captain.
Malone earned his degree in geography with a concentration in geosciences from Rowan in 2014 and received a Master's in education in adolescence urban education – social studies from LIU in 2018.
